messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] realtime-p99-latency-regression on /v2/chat/completions. p95=2.42s (SLO=250ms), p99=9.70s (SLO=1s). Source: grafana panel 'realtime-latency-overview'. Paging eng-oncall.

jamie: Paging @priya and @hong. Spike started at ~15:08 UTC, sharp rise in tail. Noting a recent canary deploy of redwood-llama-7b-q4 at 15:05.

priya: I'm on call. pulling up traces and profiler.

hong: Joining. Quick check: traffic QPS steady, but mean token-length +30% for the affected route.

jamie: customer-ops: any support noise?

customer-ops: multiple customers reported streaming cutouts and increased 504s around 15:09. Affected tenants: filing-prod, realtime-chat, telemetry-ingest. Error-rate for realtime-chat jumped 0.4% -> 12%.

priya: dash notes: per-shard request latency for pool 'alpha-gpus' shows a step where kernel-selection time spiked, and nvlink io wait jumped. KV cache hit-rate dropped 0.88 -> 0.35. Many "cache_eviction" log lines during 15:05-15:12.

hong: I'm tailing model runtime logs on gpu-node-03: seeing repeated "kernel_compile: miss" and then "fallback_to_slow_kernel". Also a few 'epoll timeout' entries aligning with client disconnects.

ops-bot: Deploy event: deploy_id=depl-77f started at 15:05 by ci-pipeline. Artifact: redwood-llama-7b-q4. Canary 10% traffic.

jamie: hypothesis: new quantized kernels caused kernel-cache churn + heavy compile IO, causing NVLink starvation and causing streaming stalls -> tail latency.

priya: mitigation plan proposed: 1) scale up canary pool temporarily to spread compile load, 2) enable fallback routing to redwood-llama-7b-compat for streaming-tenants, 3) throttle background batch jobs. Thoughts?

hong: I can scale up the canary pool by adding two spare nodes (gpu-node-04/05) from spare capacity. That should parallelize compilation and reduce hot-spotting. Initiating now.

jamie: also please apply request-level circuit-breaker for any single connection > 30s. 4) consider immediate rollback if no improvement in 5m.

ops-bot: Pool scale action queued: add_nodes(gpu-pool-alpha, [gpu-node-04,gpu-node-05]) by hong.

priya: after adding nodes p95 dropped slightly to 1.1s, p99 still ~3.6s. KV cache warming still slow.

hong: enabling fallback routing for three high-impact tenants to redwood-llama-7b-compat now.

jamie: fallback routing in place. Observed streaming success rate for fallback tenants improved immediately. Global p95=620ms, p99=1.6s.

customer-ops: affected tenant alerting: telemetry-ingest recovered after fallback; filing-prod still sees elevated latencies but improved errors.

priya: we're going to avoid full rollback for now since fallback + scale reduced customer impact. But we need root cause: kernel cache thrash + KV cold misses—likely because quantized kernel variants added many new kernel files, causing disk IO and compile queuing.

hong: I pulled filesystem iostat: spike in metadata ops and small-file writes during 15:05-15:11. NVMe SMART ok, but docker layer writes for /opt/kernels high.

jamie: next immediate actions: 1) add canary pre-warm step to compile kernels (offline warm) before traffic, 2) add KV cache warm-up for prime prompt set, 3) update rollout docs to include disk io check for new kernel artifacts. Priya, hong take action items.

priya: creating incident doc now and will collect traces. Uploading profiler snapshots and tcpdumps to s3://redwood-incidents/1991234567/ (profiles.tar.gz, tcpdumps/).

hong: saving node logs and iostat: s3 upload started. Also saving deploy artifact list and canary config.

ops-bot: Canary can be paused by: /deploy pause depl-77f.

jamie: we'll leave the canary running but gated with traffic fallback. If p99 < 1.2s consistently for 10m we'll resume gradual rollout with canary-warm steps. Otherwise, escalate to rollback.

priya: current metrics 5m after mitigations: p95=340ms, p99=940ms. Streaming stalls down to baseline.

jamie: handing off on-call to @priya at 16:00 UTC. Priya keep monitoring and file postmortem with follow-ups: K1 (canary-warm job), K2 (kernel artifact size limit + precompile), K3 (add NVMe/metadata metrics to canary health).

eng-oncall: ack. I'll monitor alerting and disable noisy alarms.

customer-ops: we're notifying enterprise customers who tagged offline webhooks. No major SLA breaches yet but several degraded experiences; CS alerted.

jamie: thanks everyone. Closing active page, thread remains open for notes and uploads. :thumbsup:
